concept_name: Hybridisation: One Dial — s-Character — Sets Both the Orbital's Shape and Its Angle
source_book: NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Ch.4 'Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure', §4.6 — valence bond theory and hybridisation of s and p orbitals (sp, sp², sp³) — chapter-index scope reference only; teaching, sequence, and phrasing authored from first principles. Every shape, angle, tip length and probability below is DERIVED from psi_h = -c_s psi_2s + c_p psi_2p on the same exact hydrogenic radial functions the shipped atomic_orbitals_s_p_d evaluates, and was solved independently BEFORE any renderer code existed (docs/concepts/chemistry/hybridisation_physics_block.md), with a control reproducing that concept's already-shipped 482 pm 2p tip. NCERT Exemplar Ch.4 consulted for the misconception belief only (that carbon bonds with its 2s and 2p orbitals unchanged, predicting three bonds at 90° and one odd one out); no problem text, figure, or worked example imported. Sixth chemistry concept through the pipeline, second on the field_3d orbital_shapes surface.

real_world_anchor.primary: Every carbon atom in every living thing is hybridised. The difference between the graphite in a pencil and the diamond in a drill bit is nothing but which hybrid carbon chose: flat sp² sheets that slide over each other, or a rigid sp³ tetrahedral lattice. Same element, same nucleus, same electrons — different angle.
real_world_anchor.secondary: The 109.5° tetrahedral angle is why water is bent, why fats have kinks in them, and why a protein folds the way it does. Almost every three-dimensional shape in chemistry traces back to how much s a bonding orbital carries.

schar.name: s-character — the fraction of the hybrid built from the 2s orbital (f = c_s²)

formulas.angle_law: cos(theta) = -f / (1 - f), where f = s-character. f = 0 -> 90 deg; f = 1/4 -> 109.47 deg; f = 1/3 -> 120 deg; f = 1/2 -> 180 deg.
formulas.hybrid_wavefunction: psi_h = -c_s psi_2s + c_p psi_2p, with c_s^2 + c_p^2 = 1 and f = c_s^2. The leading minus is the textbook convention and is load-bearing: R_20 is negative for rho > 2, so +c_s would place 82.5% of the electron behind the atom.
formulas.orthonormality: <h_i|h_j> = f + (1 - f)(a_i . a_j), which is 1 for i = j and 0 for i != j at the authored directions.

constraints: Each hybrid set is normalised and mutually orthogonal — verified numerically (max off-diagonal overlap 5.6e-17).
The number of hybrid orbitals out always equals the number of atomic orbitals in: 1s + 1p = 2 sp; 1s + 2p = 3 sp²; 1s + 3p = 4 sp³.
An arbitrary interorbital angle is realisable by EQUIVALENT hybrids only for a set of two. Three and four equivalent hybrids are locked to 120° and 109.47° respectively.
Every hybrid of the n = 2 shell has energy -3.40 eV at Z = 1, because 2s and 2p are degenerate in hydrogen; hybridisation redistributes direction, never total energy.

aha_moment.statement: One dial, the s-character, sets the angle; 109.5 degrees is where it lands.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: the s-character sweeps from 0 to one half while the live angle readout climbs continuously through 109.5 and 120 to 180, and each lobe visibly grows more lopsided as it goes — one control, two effects, neither scripted separately

STATE_1.title: Carbon's own orbitals predict the wrong molecule
STATE_1.motion_delta: the three 2p orbitals arrive one axis at a time, and every angle between them is a right angle

misconception_watch.belief: Carbon bonds using its 2s and three 2p orbitals exactly as they are, so methane should have three bonds at 90° from the p orbitals plus one different bond from the s.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The three 2p orbitals are stamped onto their axes one at a time and stay there, mutually perpendicular. The picture that results predicts three bonds at 90° and one odd one out — and methane has four identical bonds at 109.5°.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The orbitals carbon starts with cannot make four identical bonds, so they are not the orbitals carbon bonds with.

tts_sentences.text_en: Carbon has three 2p orbitals, and they lie on three perpendicular axes.
Watch them arrive. Every angle between them is a right angle, ninety degrees.
But methane has four identical bonds at a hundred and nine point five degrees. These orbitals cannot make that molecule.

STATE_2.title: Mix one s into one p and a new shape appears
STATE_2.motion_delta: the spherical 2s dissolves into the dumbbell, which swells at one end and shrinks at the other

tts_sentences.text_en: Now mix. Take the spherical 2s and one dumbbell-shaped 2p, and combine them into a single orbital.
The sphere is consumed and the dumbbell stops being symmetric. One end swells, the other shrinks away.
That lopsided shape is a hybrid orbital. Half s, half p, and identical to neither.

STATE_3.title: The big lobe is where the bond forms
STATE_3.motion_delta: the second sp hybrid grows in pointing exactly opposite, and the readout counts what sits on the bonding side

tts_sentences.text_en: Mixing one s with one p gives two hybrids, not one, and the second points exactly opposite the first.
Look at the readout. Almost eighty-eight percent of this electron sits on the big-lobe side.
That concentration is the point: a hybrid reaches further toward its neighbour, so it bonds better.

STATE_4.title: Mix in a second p and the angle closes to 120°
STATE_4.motion_delta: three hybrids appear in one flat plane, 120° apart instead of 180°

scene_composition.text: one s + two p = three sp²

tts_sentences.text_en: Mix the same s with two p orbitals instead of one, and three hybrids come out.
They lie flat in a single plane, spaced a hundred and twenty degrees apart. These are sp two hybrids.
Notice the count never breaks. Orbitals in, orbitals out, always equal.

STATE_5.title: All three p, and the answer to methane appears
STATE_5.motion_delta: a fourth hybrid lifts out of the plane and the set becomes the three-dimensional tetrahedron methane actually has

misconception_watch.belief: The four bonds of methane are still three p bonds and one s bond, just drawn differently.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The four sp3 hybrids assemble from the nucleus outward and settle at 109.5 degrees, all four the same size and the same shape. The opening state's three mutually perpendicular p orbitals had three of one kind and nowhere for a fourth to go.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: All four sp³ hybrids are identical, which is exactly what three p plus one s could never be.

tts_sentences.text_en: Now use all three p orbitals. One s plus three p gives four hybrids.
The fourth cannot stay in the plane, so the set lifts into three dimensions and settles at a hundred and nine point five degrees.
Compare that with the right angles we started from. These four are identical, and that is methane.

STATE_6.title: One dial sets the angle — and 109.5° is just where it lands
STATE_6.motion_delta: s-character rises from zero to a half and the angle opens continuously from 90° through 109.5° and 120° to 180°

tts_sentences.text_en: Here is the rule underneath all three. Sweep the s-character upward and watch the angle.
It opens smoothly from ninety degrees, through a hundred and nine point five, then a hundred and twenty, to a hundred and eighty.
The three named hybrids are just the stops where this dial makes the lobes equivalent.

STATE_7.title: The small back lobe is real, and it matters later
STATE_7.motion_delta: the lobe we have been drawing stays put while the omitted rear lobe grows out of the nucleus behind it

tts_sentences.text_en: Every picture so far drew only the big lobe. Watch what we left out grow in behind the nucleus.
The readout measures the split directly: about eighty-two percent of the electron in front, seventeen behind.
Remember it. That rear lobe is the door an attacking group uses when a bond is later broken from behind.

STATE_8.title: Explore — turn the dial and pick a hybrid
STATE_8.motion_delta: the teacher picks a hybrid and turns it; the set spins continuously

tts_sentences.text_en: Yours now. Pick any of the three hybrids and turn it, and read the angle its lobes make.
Count the lobes each one has, and check the angle against the shape you would expect.

regeneration_variants.label: Same s-character dial, nitrogen instead of carbon (the lone pair takes a hybrid too)
regeneration_variants.physical_world: Nitrogen in ammonia is also sp3 hybridised, but one of its four hybrids holds a lone pair instead of a bond, which is why ammonia's H-N-H angle is 107 degrees rather than the ideal 109.5.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical reasoning: one s mixed with three p gives four equivalent hybrids at the angle cos(theta) = -f/(1-f) returns for f = 1/4. What changes is only which hybrids get bonding partners, never how the hybrids themselves are built.
